name: Dzogchen (Great Perfection)
note: Teaching and practice lineage, not a separate institution; also held in Bön and taught across Rimé.

name: Karma Kagyu
note: Largest Kagyu branch, led by the Karmapas.

name: Drikung Kagyu
note: Founded by Jigten Sumgön.

name: Drukpa Kagyu
note: State tradition of Bhutan.

name: Shangpa Kagyu
note: Separate lineage from Niguma and Sukhasiddhi, revived by Kalu Rinpoche.

name: Mahamudra (the Great Seal)
note: Practice lineage at the heart of Kagyu, also taught in Gelug.

name: Sakya
note: Lamdre (path and its fruit) teachings; led by the Khön family.

name: FPMT (Foundation for the Preservation of the Mahayana Tradition)
note: International Gelug network founded by Lama Yeshe and Lama Zopa.

name: Jonang
note: Known for shentong (other-emptiness) and Kalachakra; suppressed in central Tibet in the 17th c. and survives in Amdo.

name: Bön (Yungdrung Bön)
note: Tibet's indigenous religion. It is not a Buddhist school, but it shares its institutions and Dzogchen with Buddhism. Placed here for browsing only.

name: Rimé (non-sectarian) movement
note: An ecumenical revival across Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Jonang, not a school.

name: Shambhala
note: Trungpa's secular "warrior" path; Pema Chödrön trained in it.

name: Chan
note: Chinese meditation school, root of Zen, Seon and Thiền.

name: Linji (Rinzai) line of Chan
note: Huatou / gong'an practice.

name: Caodong (Soto) line of Chan
note: Silent illumination (mozhao).

name: Dharma Drum Mountain
note: Taiwanese Chan organisation of Sheng Yen holding both Linji and Caodong lines.

name: Sanbo Zen (Sanbo Kyodan)
note: Lay-oriented school combining Soto and Rinzai koan curricula.

name: White Plum Asanga
note: Maezumi's lineage network (Soto with Rinzai koan study).

name: Seon (Korean Zen)
note: Korean Chan; Jogye order; Kwan Um School in the West.

name: Kwan Um School of Zen
note: International Seon school of Seung Sahn.

name: Thiền (Vietnamese Zen)
note: Vietnamese Chan; Plum Village is its best-known modern form.

name: Order of Buddhist Contemplatives
note: Shasta Abbey tradition founded by Houn Jiyu-Kennett.

name: Ordinary Mind Zen
note: Joko Beck's psychologically oriented lineage.

name: Tiantai
note: Lotus Sutra school; threefold truth; zhiguan (calming and contemplation).

name: Tendai
note: Japanese Tiantai, which also includes esoteric (taimitsu), Pure Land and Zen elements.

name: Huayan (Kegon)
note: Avatamsaka school; interpenetration of all phenomena.

name: Pure Land
note: Devotion to Amitabha and rebirth in Sukhavati.

name: Jōdo-shū
note: Honen's school.

name: Jōdo Shinshū (Shin Buddhism)
note: Shinran's school; Buddhist Churches of America in the US.

name: East Asian esoteric Buddhism
note: Chinese Zhenyan and its Japanese heirs.

name: Shingon
note: Kukai's esoteric school.
